sentences.text: Emergency arrangements define who may direct an incident, who supports rescue, and who may authorize a return to work.
The Shore Control Room maintains the incident log and provides a single operational point of contact for offshore teams.
The Rescue Coordinator leads rescue planning and coordinates requests for external assistance.
The Field Supervisor directs personnel at the affected work site until control is formally transferred.
The Vessel Master retains authority over vessel safety, navigation, and decisions to approach or withdraw from a casualty.
The HSE Officer advises on personnel hazards, rescue procedures, and the use of emergency equipment.
The Marine Coordinator maintains awareness of vessel locations, access constraints, and available marine support.
The Personnel Tracking Console supports personnel accounting, but the incident lead verifies headcounts with the teams involved.
Crew Transfer Vessel operations are suspended when sea conditions, visibility, or transfer arrangements exceed approved limits.
A Daughter Craft may support a local response only when its crew, equipment, and launch conditions are suitable.
A Service Operations Vessel may provide accommodation, medical support, and a stable platform when its position and capability permit.
The Helideck is used for evacuation only when aviation conditions, deck readiness, and receiving arrangements are acceptable.
The Weather Service provides forecast information for planning, while operational decisions account for observed local conditions.
The Metocean Buoy provides site measurements that help assess whether a planned response remains feasible.
The Weather Analyst interprets forecast uncertainty and communicates material changes to the Rescue Coordinator.
The Operations Radio Console supports communications between the Shore Control Room, vessels, and offshore work teams.
Emergency Generator readiness is checked as part of site emergency preparedness and restoration planning.
The Fire Detection Panel provides alarm indications that responders use alongside direct reports from personnel on site.
The Control Engineer supports remote shutdown actions when communications and equipment status allow safe intervention.
Electrical recovery work requires qualified personnel, verified isolation, and a safe means of access before hands-on activity begins.
Recovery of injured or incapacitated personnel may be delayed by vessel motion, limited access, lifting capacity, or deteriorating conditions.
Offshore recovery plans identify the point at which continued response would expose rescuers to unacceptable risk.
If conditions exceed the approved operating envelope, the Vessel Master may withdraw and the Rescue Coordinator revises the response plan.
After an incident, personnel are accounted for, hazards are reassessed, and restart authority is assigned before normal work resumes.
